preamble: Click loss replaces the alveolar click [ǃ] with the plain velar stop [k]: the anterior (alveolar) closure and the velaric suction are given up, and only the rear velar closure survives. Traill & Vossen (1997) set up ǃ → k (alongside palatal ǂ → c) as the regular replacement pattern in Eastern Kalahari Khoe, where alveolar and palatal clicks are lost in many cognates while dental and lateral clicks survive. In the Cua–Kua–Tsua continuum of Botswana, words with [ǃ] in click-retaining Gǀui show [k] in Cua and Tsua, often with loss of the click's nasal or uvular accompaniment as well. The change is confined to this one subgroup, so it is rare.

examples.note: The nasal alveolar click is replaced by plain [k], with denasalization; Kua has ŋare with a velar nasal instead.
Same correspondence; Kua again has ŋua.

examples.to: kanu 'to carry soft matter on the shoulder'
examples.note: The alveolar click and its uvular-ejective accompaniment are both lost.
Cua and Tsua share the [k] reflex, against Kua ŋare and click-retaining Gǀui.
